target.title: feat(android): platform trust for public gateway certs + manual fingerprint pinning
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Android app pins a TLS fingerprint for every gateway, including hosts with publicly valid certificates. For a Tailscale Funnel gateway on `*.ts.net` with a Let's Encrypt cert, that means a "fingerprint changed" re-verification prompt every 60–90 day renewal — recurring friction that trains users to click through security prompts. Separately, when the TLS probe failed with no stored pin, connecting hard-failed with no escape hatch, and a malformed stored pin silently degraded instead of failing closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Platform trust for public certs.** Before prompting, the probe performs a real handshake against the system CA store with `endpointIdentificationAlgorithm="HTTPS"` and SNI. If the chain validates and the hostname matches, the connection uses platform trust — no pin stored, no prompt, renewals just work. A conservative candidate classifier (rejects `.local`, IPv4/IPv6 literals, single-label and malformed hostnames) keeps LAN endpoints on the existing pin flow.
- **Existing pins stay authoritative.** A valid public chain never silently clears a user-accepted pin. On mismatch with a system-trusted cert, the changed-pin prompt gains an explicit "Use system trust" choice; picking it clears the pin once, after which renewals are automatic. Replacing a pin always requires explicit confirmation.
- **Discovery cannot become identity.** Saved discovered endpoints still require a stored fingerprint for reconnect eligibility — mDNS advertisements are attacker-controllable on the LAN, and a DNS-shaped advertised host with the attacker's own valid cert must not inherit a saved gateway's credentials.
- **Out-of-band manual pinning.** When the probe can't capture a certificate, the trust dialog accepts a pasted SHA-256 fingerprint obtained on the gateway host (tolerates `sha256:` prefixes, colons, whitespace, case; requires 64 hex), then enforces it on connect — stronger verification than eyeball-TOFU, and an escape hatch where there was a dead end.
- Hardening along the way: malformed stored pins now fail closed at handshake time; both probe attempts share one connect+handshake budget so a TCP-accepting, TLS-stalling host cannot double probe latency; the trust decision is a closed sealed type (`SystemTrusted` / `PinnedTrust` / `PromptRequired` / `Failed`).

## User Impact

Funnel/public-cert gateways connect without fingerprint ceremony and stop re-prompting on cert renewals. LAN and IP gateways keep trust-on-first-use pinning with the existing first-seen and changed-pin dialogs. Users who deliberately pinned a public host keep their pin unless they explicitly switch. Two new user-facing strings, translated across all 21 locales.

## Evidence

- `GatewayTlsTest` (trust-decision matrix incl. supersession rows, candidate classifier, fingerprint normalizer, probe-budget splitting), `GatewayBootstrapAuthTest`, `GatewaySessionCustomHeadersTest`: green on both Play and ThirdParty flavors (14 + 51 + 2 per flavor).
- `:app:ktlintCheck`, `android-app-i18n` check, `git diff --check`: green.
- Structured autoreview: three rounds; four accepted findings fixed (two P1s — discovery-eligibility identity binding, silent pin supersession — plus fail-closed pin handling and probe-latency amplification); final round clean: "consistently adds Android platform trust for eligible DNS gateways while preserving existing certificate pins."
- All `resolveTlsParams` call sites verified `allowTOFU=false`, so the system-trust path connects with platform trust and real hostname verification (no TOFU fallback).

target.title: fix: distinct Responses tool-call ids for repeated native Kimi calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where users on the `openai-responses` API path would stop getting any agent replies at all once a session called the same tool at the same call-index more than once (a common pattern — e.g. a `gateway`/status-check tool invoked first in several separate turns). Every subsequent turn on that session failed before producing a reply, with the gateway logging `invalid_replay_transcript: ... dangling_tool_call toolCallId=call_<hash>`. The session was effectively bricked until manually truncated or reset.

Observed on `moonshotai/kimi-k2.5` via OpenRouter, which is what my agent was routed to at the time. The bug isn't model-specific, though — it's in OpenClaw's own id normalizer for the `openai-responses` wire format, so it reproduces for any model/provider combination that goes through that API shape and reuses native `functions.<tool>:<index>|fc_*`-style ids across turns.

## Why This Change Was Made

`normalizeOpenAIResponsesFunctionCallId` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/openai.ts`) rewrites native tool-call ids like `functions.gateway:0|fc_tmp_kegospxl46` into `call_*` ids the OpenAI Responses API accepts. It splits the id into a `callId` half (`functions.gateway:0`) and an `itemId` half (`fc_tmp_kegospxl46`), but only hashed the `callId` half when generating the `call_*` id. Since `callId` is just `<toolName>:<callIndexInTurn>`, it repeats across turns whenever the same tool is called at the same position — so every occurrence collapsed to the identical `call_*` id, corrupting replay once two or more calls collided in the same session history.

The fix hashes the full `callId|itemId` pairing (falling back to `callId` alone when there is no `itemId`), so repeated native ids that share a `callId` now normalize to distinct ids while still resolving consistently between the assistant tool-call and its matching tool-result.

## User Impact

Sessions on `openai-responses`-backed providers no longer get permanently stuck after the same tool is called at the same index more than once in a conversation — replies keep working instead of failing on every turn with a replay error.

## Evidence

- [x] Mark as AI-assisted in the PR title or description — root-caused and fixed with an AI coding assistant (Claude Code) after diagnosing the issue on a personal OpenClaw instance; I reviewed and understand the change.

**Full before/after runtime proof (linked artifact):** https://gist.github.com/christiandesantis/b1cee60d56319d2d80013310a0ba9cb8 — verbatim `openclaw logs`/`openclaw sessions list --json`/`openclaw agent --json` output from my own instance: session `agent:main:main` (`980f8d6e-c602-4540-b54d-20602bab3d0f`) status `"failed"` before the patch with the repeated `dangling_tool_call` error, then `"done"` after, plus the `workspace.test.ts` CI-flake repro from below. Nothing in it is sensitive — just error metadata, session/run ids, and JSON structure, no personal data.

**Root cause repro** (standalone, no runtime needed):
```
$ node -e 'console.log(require("crypto").createHash("sha256").update("functions.gateway:0").digest("hex").slice(0,10))'
24933ffc9b
```
This matches the exact `toolCallId` from the failure below — proving the collision is `sha256("functions.gateway:0")`, i.e. the `callId` half alone, independent of which specific call produced it.

**Before fix** — real gateway log from my own OpenClaw instance, `agent:main:main` session, every single turn failing identically:
```
$ openclaw logs
2026-07-18T14:46:46.695-04:00 error diagnostic lane task error: lane=main durationMs=253 error="Error: invalid_replay_transcript: OpenAI Responses replay contains dangling_tool_call toolCallId=call_functions_gateway_0_24933ffc9b at message index 18"
2026-07-18T14:46:46.697-04:00 error diagnostic lane task error: lane=session:agent:main:main durationMs=255 error="Error: invalid_replay_transcript: OpenAI Responses replay contains dangling_tool_call toolCallId=call_functions_gateway_0_24933ffc9b at message index 18"
2026-07-18T14:46:46.701-04:00 error Embedded agent failed before reply: invalid_replay_transcript: OpenAI Responses replay contains dangling_tool_call toolCallId=call_functions_gateway_0_24933ffc9b at message index 18
```
The identical error (same `toolCallId`) repeated on every retry over the following ~10 minutes (14:50:21, 14:50:52, 14:51:25, 14:52:26, 14:54:28) — the session never recovered on its own.

**After fix** — same corrupted session, replayed through the patched code (hotpatched compiled output + gateway restart), triggered via `openclaw agent --session-key "agent:main:main" --agent main -m "..." --json`:
```json
"replayInvalid": false,
"livenessState": "working",
"stopReason": "stop",
"executionTrace": {
  "winnerProvider": "openrouter",
  "winnerModel": "moonshotai/kimi-k3",
  "attempts": [{ "provider": "openrouter", "model": "moonshotai/kimi-k3", "result": "success", "stage": "assistant" }],
  "fallbackUsed": false,
  "runner": "embedded"
}
```
Followed by a clean `openclaw logs` tail with no further `dangling_tool_call`/`invalid_replay_transcript` entries and a normal `run ... ended with stopReason=stop` line — the previously-bricked session now completes turns normally. (The response happened to land on `kimi-k3` since the default model had moved on by the time I re-tested — unrelated to the fix, which is model-agnostic.)

**Automated proof:**
- Added `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/openai.test.ts`, a focused regression test asserting two native ids that share a `callId` but differ only in `itemId` now normalize to distinct `call_*` ids, with each `toolResult` still resolving to the matching (now-distinct) `toolCall`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/openai.test.ts` — passes.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — both clean.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/openai.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/openai.test.ts` — 0 warnings, 0 errors (fixed a `no-shadow` finding from the initial version of the test).
- `pnpm format` — clean, no diff beyond the intended change.

- I don't have a shareable session log for the AI-assisted diagnosis/fix (local troubleshooting session, not something I captured for export), happy to describe the exact steps if useful for review.
- `autoreview` skill: not run — it isn't available to me as an external contributor without OpenClaw's internal tooling access.

target.title: fix(ui): keep agent avatar initials on grapheme clusters
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI agent avatar fallbacks used `.slice(0, 1)` on the agent name/id.
Names starting with a flag emoji (`🇺🇸Team`) or ZWJ sequence (`👨‍💻Dev`) were
cut mid-cluster and rendered as replacement characters / incomplete glyphs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `resolveFallbackAvatarInitial` using `Intl.Segmenter` grapheme granularity
(with `Array.from` fallback when Segmenter is unavailable), and use it in the
three agent avatar fallback call sites. Keep the prior locale-independent
`toUpperCase()` casing contract (not `toLocaleUpperCase()`).

## User Impact

**Before:** Agent names beginning with multi-code-point emoji produced broken
avatar initials.

**After:** Fallback avatars keep a complete grapheme (flag / ZWJ emoji / letter)
with the same ASCII casing behavior as before.

## Evidence

- Changed: `ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts`, `ui/src/lib/agents/display.test.ts`,
  `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts`,
  `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-agent-menu.ts`,
  `ui/src/pages/agents/panels-overview.ts`,
  `ui/src/test-helpers/app-sidebar-cases/agent-menu.ts`
- Production path: sidebar agent card / agent menu / agents overview identity
  editor → `resolveFallbackAvatarInitial` when no text avatar is configured
- Compatibility: ASCII initials still uppercased via `toUpperCase()`; empty
  labels become `?`

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Mounted Control UI sidebar renders `🇺🇸` in the agent-chip avatar slot for
`identity.name = "🇺🇸Team"`, and menu switch rows render `🇺🇸` / `👨‍💻` for
flag- and ZWJ-leading agent names.

### Canonical reachability path

Control UI agent chip / menu / overview →
`resolveAgentTextAvatar(...) ?? resolveFallbackAvatarInitial(label)` →
`.sidebar-agent-card__avatar-text` / `.sidebar-agent-section__avatar`

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Same Segmenter pattern as `ui/src/pages/plugins/presentation.ts`
`takeGraphemes`; no new config.

### Real environment tested

Local trusted source checkout at PR head; jsdom Control UI component mount via
existing `mountSidebar` harness (same production Lit templates as the live
sidebar); Node via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts \
  -t "complete flag and ZWJ" --reporter=verbose
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/agents/display.test.ts \
  -t "flag and ZWJ|locale-independent" --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

Rendered Control UI avatar slot (production templates):

```text
✓ AppSidebar agent chip > renders complete flag and ZWJ graphemes in the agent chip avatar slot
  expect(...avatar-text...).toBe("🇺🇸")
  expect(...menu flag avatar...).toBe("🇺🇸")
  expect(...menu ZWJ avatar...).toBe("👨‍💻")
```

Helper + casing contract:

```text
✓ keeps flag and ZWJ emoji clusters intact
✓ keeps locale-independent ASCII casing (Turkish i)
```

### Observed result after fix

The live sidebar agent-chip and agent-menu avatar slots render complete flag
and ZWJ graphemes instead of UTF-16-sliced fragments, without changing the
prior `toUpperCase()` casing contract.

target.title: feat(android): accept audio and document attachments via share sheet and composer
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Android app's share-sheet intake only accepted `text/*` and `image/*`, and the composer could only attach images — even though the send pipeline already supports audio and file attachment types (voice notes prove the audio path) and the gateway happily accepts non-image attachments by offloading them to the media store for agent-side reads. Sharing a PDF, a voice memo, or a CSV from another app into OpenClaw was simply impossible on Android.

## Why This Change Was Made

Close the intake gap without touching the transport: add `ACTION_SEND`/`ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE` filters for `audio/*` and a curated document set (PDF, the OOXML trio, CSV, Markdown — deliberately not blanket `application/*`), and a document/audio picker next to the existing image picker in the composer.

Intake stays hardened the same way image shares already were, plus new guards where non-image bytes need them:

- code-side mime allowlist (manifest filters are advisory; a hostile sender can lie in `intent.type`) with provider-type revalidation at load time while the URI grant is live — a type that changes between parse and load is rejected;
- `content://`-scheme enforcement, dedupe, and the 8-item cap with dropped-count reporting preserved;
- bounded streaming reads with per-kind size budgets (images keep the JPEG limiter; audio/documents cap at the outbox command attachment limit) and display-name sanitization;
- share parsing moved off the main thread behind a bounded slot queue with the composer-owner captured up front, so owner-migration races behave exactly like the existing image path;
- draft-not-autosend unchanged: shared content stages into the composer and sending still requires an explicit tap.

## User Impact

Android users can now share audio files and documents (PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, CSV, Markdown) into OpenClaw from any app's share sheet, and attach them from inside the chat composer. Oversized or unsupported items are dropped with the same visible notice behavior images use today.

## Evidence

- `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` for `ShareLaunchTest` (audio single/multiple, document single, mixed batch, `application/octet-stream` rejection, scheme rejection, caps) and `ChatComposerDraftTest` (per-kind budget admission): green.
- `:app:compilePlayDebugKotlin` + `:app:ktlintCheck`: green.
- Structured autoreview: clean — "consistently extends share parsing, bounded loading, composer admission, owner-safe queueing, and picker support … no concrete regression or exploitable defect."
- Size caps aligned with `OUTBOX_MAX_COMMAND_ATTACHMENT_BYTES` (8 MiB) under the gateway's 20 MB default attachment ceiling (`chat-attachments.ts`).

target.title: fix(agents): strip MiniMax stream-boundary marker from transport payload text
target.body:
## Summary

Closes #104403 — a MiniMax-portal stream-boundary marker (`ESC[e~[` / `[e~[`) leaked into `assistantTexts[0]`, the trajectory JSONL, and the next-turn `finalPromptText`, so every assistant reply ended with a stray token.

## Root cause

`sanitizeTransportPayloadText` only stripped malformed surrogate pairs. The MiniMax portal injects a terminal/escape stream-boundary marker into assistant text on the anthropic-messages transport; nothing removed it, so it propagated to every downstream consumer.

## Fix

- `src/agents/transport-stream-shared.ts`: `sanitizeTransportPayloadText` now also strips ANSI/terminal escape sequences (reusing `stripAnsiSequences`) and the MiniMax boundary marker. Both the anthropic-messages and openai-responses transports call this helper, so the noise is removed at the transport layer where it actually enters `assistantTexts`.
- This complements the channel-layer stripping in #105243 rather than duplicating it.

## Verification

- `vitest run --pool forks src/agents/transport-stream-shared.test.ts` — 22 passed (incl. new regression test for the ESC-prefixed marker, the bare `[e~[` form, repeated markers, and ordinary ANSI color codes).
- `oxlint` clean (0/0), `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed file.

## Note

The reporter also referenced an attached report with a suggested code diff; the core defect (marker not stripped at the transport layer) is addressed here. If maintainers want the marker handled exclusively at the channel layer instead, this transport-layer strip is harmless and defensively correct.

target.title: fix(thinking): fall back instead of erroring on unsupported adaptive level (#109351)
target.body:
## Summary

Messages from clients that send `thinking="adaptive"` as a transport default (e.g. the Apple Watch client) were rejected with `Thinking level "adaptive" is not supported for <provider>/<model>`, while the same message from the paired iOS app (which sends no override) succeeded.

`adaptive` is the **auto sentinel** — `normalizeThinkLevel` maps `"auto"` -> `"adaptive"`. It means *"pick an appropriate level"*, not *"force this exact level"*. So when a model does not support `adaptive`, the correct behavior is to fall back to a supported level, not hard-error.

## Fix

In `runPreparedReply` (`src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.ts`), the unsupported-thinking-level guard no longer treats an `adaptive` resolved level as an explicit hard-error case. The auto sentinel now always flows into the existing `resolveSupportedThinkingLevel` fallback. Explicit **concrete** levels (e.g. a real `/think xhigh` or a one-turn `xhigh` override) still hard-error exactly as before.

## Testing

- New regression test in `get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts`: an unsupported `adaptive` override falls back and runs the agent instead of erroring.
- Existing test `reports unsupported explicit one-turn thinking overrides` (concrete `xhigh`) still passes — explicit concrete levels remain hard errors.
- `vitest run --pool forks src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts` -> **101/101 pass**; oxlint 0/0; oxfmt clean.

Closes #109351

target.title: fix: distinct Responses tool-call ids for repeated native Kimi calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where users on the `openai-responses` API path would stop getting any agent replies at all once a session called the same tool at the same call-index more than once (a common pattern — e.g. a `gateway`/status-check tool invoked first in several separate turns). Every subsequent turn on that session failed before producing a reply, with the gateway logging `invalid_replay_transcript: ... dangling_tool_call toolCallId=call_<hash>`. The session was effectively bricked until manually truncated or reset.

Observed on `moonshotai/kimi-k2.5` via OpenRouter, which is what my agent was routed to at the time. The bug isn't model-specific, though — it's in OpenClaw's own id normalizer for the `openai-responses` wire format, so it reproduces for any model/provider combination that goes through that API shape and reuses native `functions.<tool>:<index>|fc_*`-style ids across turns.

## Why This Change Was Made

`normalizeOpenAIResponsesFunctionCallId` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/openai.ts`) rewrites native tool-call ids like `functions.gateway:0|fc_tmp_kegospxl46` into `call_*` ids the OpenAI Responses API accepts. It splits the id into a `callId` half (`functions.gateway:0`) and an `itemId` half (`fc_tmp_kegospxl46`), but only hashed the `callId` half when generating the `call_*` id. Since `callId` is just `<toolName>:<callIndexInTurn>`, it repeats across turns whenever the same tool is called at the same position — so every occurrence collapsed to the identical `call_*` id, corrupting replay once two or more calls collided in the same session history.

The fix hashes the full `callId|itemId` pairing (falling back to `callId` alone when there is no `itemId`), so repeated native ids that share a `callId` now normalize to distinct ids while still resolving consistently between the assistant tool-call and its matching tool-result.

## User Impact

Sessions on `openai-responses`-backed providers no longer get permanently stuck after the same tool is called at the same index more than once in a conversation — replies keep working instead of failing on every turn with a replay error.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(auto-reply): degrade gracefully when preflight compaction hard-fails
target.body:
## Summary

Closes #100778 — a preflight compaction LLM failure (timeout, rate limit, provider 5xx) aborted the whole reply and left the Control UI/webchat Composer permanently in a "terminated" state; the user could not send another message without a page refresh.

## Root cause

`runPreflightCompactionIfNeeded` threw on a non-`ok` compaction result. The throw propagated to the chat dispatch-error lifecycle, which cleared the chat run and left the Composer "killed". The code itself documents the intent that preflight compaction is a guardrail, not a hard dependency.

## Fix

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts`: both failure throw sites in `runPreflightCompactionIfNeeded` now skip compaction and return the session entry (continuing the agent run) instead of throwing. The failure is still logged via `logVerbose`.
- Benign skip reasons (`below_threshold`, `no_compactable_entries`, `already_compacted_recently`) are unchanged.

## Verification

- `vitest run --pool forks src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.preflight-stale-tokens.test.ts` — 3 passed (incl. new regression test asserting a hard compaction failure resolves without throwing and returns the entry).
- `oxlint` clean (0/0), `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed file.

## Note

This makes the failure path non-fatal (degrade by skipping compaction), matching the documented "guardrail, not a hard dependency" intent. If maintainers prefer a different recovery (e.g. surfacing an actionable error toast while keeping the Composer enabled), that can layer on top of this change.

target.title: fix(telegram): surface draft stream delivery failures at warn level
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Telegram draft/preview streaming fails — `sendMessage`/`editMessageText` rejections, a missing message id from `sendMessage`, or preview cleanup failures — the failure is reported only through `logVerbose`. In the default configuration these lines never reach the logs: the preview stream silently stops and the operator sees nothing. This is worst in `progress` stream mode, where the activity window is the only visible delivery surface, so a dead draft stream looks like the bot silently ignoring the user, with no trace to debug from.

Observed on a production gateway: intermittent "bot went quiet" reports that took a verbose-logging session to trace back to `telegram stream preview failed: ...` errors that had been happening invisibly.

Closes #111064

## Why This Change Was Made

`createTelegramDraftController` wired the draft stream's `warn` callback to `logVerbose` (`extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch-draft.ts`). The failure messages themselves originate in `extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.ts` ("telegram stream preview failed: ...", "telegram stream preview stopped (missing message id from sendMessage)", "telegram stream preview cleanup failed: ...", "telegram stream preview cleanup was not confirmed ..."), so the stream already distinguishes warn-worthy failures from verbose progress logging — the dispatch wiring just discarded that distinction.

The fix routes the `warn` callback through the plugin's standard subsystem logger (`createSubsystemLogger("telegram/draft-stream")`) at warn level, attaching `lane` (answer/reasoning), `chatId`, and `threadId` so a failure can be tied to a specific chat and delivery lane. The verbose `log` callback is unchanged, and no delivery behavior changes — this is logging-only.

## User Impact

Operators now see draft/preview delivery failures in default logs with enough context to identify the affected chat and lane, instead of a silently stalled bot. No change to message delivery, retries, or stream behavior.

## Evidence

- New test in the existing dispatch failure harness: `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.draft-failures-progress.test.ts` — "routes draft stream failures to the warn-level telegram logger with lane context" proves the warn callback passed to `createTelegramDraftStream` emits on the `telegram/draft-stream` subsystem logger at warn level with `{ lane, chatId, threadId }`, not on the verbose path.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.draft-failures-progress.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.test.ts` — 103 passed.
- `.../bot-message-dispatch.draft-finalization.test.ts .../bot-message-dispatch.draft-rotation.test.ts` — 27 passed.
- Extensions tsgo lane: no errors in touched files (only pre-existing, unrelated `packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts` errors present at base).
- The equivalent patch has been running on a production gateway since 2026-07-11 and has surfaced real preview failures that were previously invisible.

This PR was AI-assisted (implemented with Claude Code; reviewed by the operator).


This fix was developed with AI assistance; the change and its validation were reviewed by the submitting author.

### Runtime proof: induced Telegram outage, BEFORE vs AFTER

**Harness.** A driver (tsx against this checkout) runs the real production bundle end to end: `createTelegramDraftController` from `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch-draft.ts` builds its draft lanes, the lanes construct the real `createTelegramDraftStream` from `extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.ts`, and the `warn`/`log` callbacks are the module's own wiring (`logVerbose` on main; the `telegram/draft-stream` subsystem logger from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env` on this branch). Logging runs at the default configuration (console level `info`, file level `info`; the state dir is isolated via `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, with only `logging.file` pointed into the harness directory). ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running the Telegram channel in polling mode against a Bot API endpoint that answers `getUpdates` immediately — notably self-hosted `telegram-bot-api` servers and some intermediary proxies — would see the ingress worker busy-spin while the chat is idle: each empty poll completes in milliseconds and the next one starts right away, pinning a CPU core and flooding the endpoint with requests. Observed in production on 2026-05-22 with a self-hosted `telegram-bot-api` server that did not hold the requested long-poll timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

The polling loop trusted the endpoint to enforce the requested long-poll timeout and had no pacing of its own. This change enforces a 1-second floor between consecutive empty `getUpdates` cycles, measured from poll start, so endpoints that honor the long-poll timeout are never delayed and non-empty polls still drain pending traffic at full speed. The wait listens to the worker stop signal, so shutdown stays immediate; error paths keep their existing backoff and `retry_after` behavior.

## User Impact

Telegram polling against fast-answering Bot API endpoints now idles at near-zero CPU instead of pinning a core. Update delivery latency is unchanged for endpoints that honor the long-poll timeout and for busy chats; the worst case for a fast-empty endpoint is one poll per second while idle.

## Evidence

- Production incident (2026-05-22): a gateway polling a self-hosted `telegram-bot-api` server spun the ingress worker at ~100% CPU while idle because the endpoint returned empty `getUpdates` responses immediately instead of holding the long poll. The same pacing, applied as a local patch, removed the spin without affecting delivery latency.
- New regression test in `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.runtime.test.ts` ("paces fast successful empty getUpdates responses") proves with fake timers that after an instant empty response the next poll does not start at 999 ms and starts exactly at the 1000 ms floor.
- Existing worker tests (durable-before-offset, retry policy) still pass, proving non-empty polls and error/backoff paths are unchanged: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.runtime.test.ts` — 8/8 passed; `extensions/telegram/src/polling-session.test.ts` — 75/75 passed.

This fix was developed with AI assistance; the change and its validation were reviewed by the submitting author.

target.title: fix(markdown): keep IR text slicing UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

**What changed**: Added surrogate pair boundary detection to `sliceMarkdownIR` in `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`. Before slicing text, start/end indices are now checked and adjusted to avoid splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs. If start lands on a low surrogate, it expands backward; if end lands on a high surrogate, it expands forward. The same adjusted boundaries are applied consistently to text, styles, links, and annotations. Empty slices (start === end) are preserved as-is — surrogate pair adjustment no longer converts them into non-empty ranges.

**What NOT changed**: No changes to the public API of `sliceMarkdownIR`, no changes to any other files, no behavioral changes for text that does not contain surrogate pairs (ASCII/ISO-8859 text is unaffected). Empty-slice callers continue to receive empty text.

Fixes #110643

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When slicing markdown IR text, the raw `start`/`end` indices may land in the middle of a UTF-16 surrogate pair, producing invalid text with a dangling high or low surrogate character. Additionally, equal start/end offsets inside a surrogate pair were incorrectly expanded into a non-empty range.

**Behavior addressed**: Ensure `sliceMarkdownIR` adjusts slice boundaries to avoid splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs, producing valid text output, while preserving empty slices (insertion points) as empty.

**Root Cause**: In `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`, `sliceMarkdownIR` passes indices directly to `String.prototype.slice()` without checking surrogate pair boundaries. Characters outside the BMP (e.g. emoji) are encoded as two UTF-16 code units (high + low surrogate), and slicing between them breaks the pair.

**Solution**: Before slicing, scan the start/end boundaries and adjust them: if `start` lands on a low surrogate, expand backward to include the full pair; if `end` lands on a high surrogate, expand forward. Apply the same adjusted boundaries consistently to text, styles, links, and annotations. When `start === end` (empty slice), skip surrogate pair adjustment to preserve the empty result.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-40-generic (Ubuntu 24.04), Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node demo-utf16.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence — direct invocation of sliceMarkdownIR logic on surrogate-pair text**:
```
============================================
PR #110643 — sliceMarkdownIR UTF-16 Safe Demo
============================================

--- Test 1: start on low surrogate ---
   Input text: "a😀b"
   Length (code units): 4
   Native slice(2, 4): "\ude00b"
   Safe slice(2, 4):   "😀b"
   Expected: "😀b"
   Match: ✓

--- Test 2: end on surrogate boundary ---
   Input text: "a😀b"
   Native slice(0, 2): "a\ud83d"
   Safe slice(0, 2):   "a😀"
   Expected: "a😀"
   Match: ✓

--- Test 3: empty slice at surrogate boundary ---
   Input text: "a😀b"
   Native slice(2, 2): ""
   Safe slice(2, 2):   ""
   Expected: "" (empty)
   Match: ✓

--- Test 4: multiple emoji ---
   Input text: "😀🎉hello😀"
   Length (code units): 11
   Safe slice(0, 4):   "😀🎉"
   Expected: "😀🎉"
   Match: ✓

--- Test 5: negative start index ---
   Input text: "ab😀cd"
   Safe slice(-3, 6): "😀cd"
   Expected: "😀cd"
   Match: ✓
```

The demo directly invokes the UTF-16 safe slicing logic and compares it against native `String.prototype.slice()`. Native slice produces lone surrogates (`\ude00b`, `a\ud83d`) when boundaries split a surrogate pair; the safe variant correctly includes the full emoji character.

**Observed result after the fix**: `sliceMarkdownIR` correctly handles surrogate pair boundaries by expanding out of the split position to include the full character, while preserving empty-slice semantics.

**What was not tested**: N/A — the fix is fully covered by the 10 unit tests.

## Tests and validation

<details>
<summary>Test output (10/10 passed)</summary>

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.10

 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > expands start boundary backward when it lands on a low surrogate
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > expands end boundary forward when it splits between HS and LS
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > preserves full text when boundaries are already clean
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > leaves boundaries unchanged when start is on a high surrogate
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > handles multiple consecutive surrogate pairs
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > handles negative start index
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > propagates adjusted boundaries to link spans
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > preserves empty slice when start === end lands inside a surrogate pair
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > preserves empty slice when start === end lands on a high surrogate
 ✓ |unit| packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts > sliceMarkdownIR surrogate pair boundaries > handles start on HS, end on LS with offset

 Test Files  1 passed (1)

```

- [X] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [X] I have updated relevant documentation

target.title: fix(plugins): deep-clone registry snapshot so nested mutations roll back (#107514)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The plugin registration transaction snapshot used a **shallow clone** (`{ ...value }` for object fields). This left nested registration objects (e.g. hook/tool/config entries) **shared by reference** with the live registry. When a transaction mutated a nested property in place and then rolled back, the snapshot's shallow copy did not capture the nested change, so the mutated state survived rollback and orphan registers stayed in the manifest cache. (#107514)

## Why This Change Was Made

`snapshotPluginRegistry` must produce a true point-in-time copy so `restorePluginRegistry` can fully revert every in-transaction change, including nested config mutations — not just top-level array pushes or field replacements. `structuredClone` is already the project-standard deep copy (used in `hooks.ts`, `installed-plugin-index-*`, etc.) and `PluginRegistry` is pure data (arrays + Maps + strings), so it clones cleanly.

## User Impact

Plugin registration install/enable timeouts that roll back no longer leave orphaned registers / stale nested config behind in the manifest cache. No behavior change for successful commits.

## Evidence

- Root cause confirmed in `src/plugins/plugin-registration-transaction.ts` `snapshotPluginRegistry` (shallow `{...value}`).
- Added regression test `rolls back nested config mutations on a registered entry (#107514)` — fails against the old shallow clone, passes with `structuredClone`.
- `pnpm lint` + `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files.
- Freshness gate: `git diff origin/main` confirms the shallow clone is still present on latest `main`; no competing open PR references #107514.

target.title: fix(transcripts): imported text can inject terminal escapes through transcripts show
target.body:
Closes #102392

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators viewing a stored transcript summary with `openclaw transcripts show` would have raw terminal control sequences replayed into their terminal when the imported transcript text contained escape bytes. A transcript line such as `ESC[2J ESC[31mADMIN APPROVED ESC[0m` could clear the screen, spoof colored status text, or emit other terminal controls the moment the summary was displayed, because the escape bytes were persisted verbatim into `summary.md` and written directly to stdout. `transcripts list` had the same sink: session titles and externally supplied session IDs were formatted into list lines unsanitized.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sanitization is applied at presentation boundaries only; canonical identity is never rewritten. `summarizeTranscripts` sanitizes the derived summary content (utterance text, speaker labels, session title) with the existing terminal-core `sanitizeTerminalText` helper, `renderTranscriptsMarkdown` sanitizes the session ID it renders into the `Session:` line, `transcripts show` sanitizes stored markdown line by line at the stdout boundary so summaries persisted before this change are also protected, and `transcripts list` sanitizes the metadata columns it prints.

`TranscriptsSummary.sessionId` keeps the raw provider-supplied session ID. `TranscriptsStore.writeSummary` uses that field to locate the existing metadata and transcript directory when the optional session descriptor is not passed, so a lossy rewrite would misplace regenerated summary artifacts under a different directory. Identity stays raw; only rendering sanitizes.

The selector printed by `transcripts list` is now the directory-backed form `YYYY-MM-DD/<safe-segment>`, the same conservative segment the store uses on disk. It is terminal-safe by construction (no control bytes can survive `safeSegment`), and `show` and `path` resolve that exact printed value in addition to the raw session ID, so the documented copy-the-selector workflow keeps working for externally supplied IDs that carry escape bytes. For ordinary session IDs the printed selector is byte-identical to before.

The raw capture in `transcript.jsonl` and the stored `metadata.json`/`summary.json` are intentionally left untouched for fidelity; they are JSON-encoded on disk, so control bytes are escaped, and the CLI JSON output paths escape them via `JSON.stringify` as well.

## User Impact

Operators can view summaries of imported or captured transcripts and list stored sessions without untrusted transcript content executing terminal control sequences in their terminal. Selectors printed by `transcripts list` can always be copied back into `transcripts show` and `transcripts path`, including for session IDs containing escape bytes. Summary artifacts regenerated without a session descriptor keep landing in the original session directory. Plain transcript content and plain session IDs render exactly as before.

## Evidence

Live before/after on the real transcripts pipeline: a hostile transcript is imported through the real manual transcript provider, persisted through the real `TranscriptsStore` (summary written without the optional session descriptor), then driven through the real `transcripts list`, `show`, and `path` commands, on identical inputs. Only `src/transcripts/summary.ts` and `src/cli/program/register.transcripts.ts` are switched between pristine `main` (4a675228af) and this patch (head 7ee6df2a21). Escape bytes are shown in `cat -v` form (`^[` is the raw ESC byte); the selector passed to `show` and `path` is copied programmatically from the first column of `list` output.

```
=== BEFORE (pristine main 4a675228af) ===
--- seed: real import -> TranscriptsStore -> writeSummary (no session descriptor) ---
{"summaryWrittenTo":".../transcripts/2026-07-16/ansi--31mprovider-0m/summary.md","summaryInOriginalDir":true}
--- openclaw transcripts list ---
2026-07-16/ansi-^[[31mprovider^[[0m	2026-07-16T10:00:00.000Z	^[[31mQ3 Board sync^[[0m	.../summary.md
--- openclaw transcripts show <selector copied from list> ---
# ^[[31mQ3 Board sync^[[0m
...
Session: ansi-^[[31mprovider^[[0m
## Overview
^[[2J^[[31mADMIN APPROVED^[[0m decision: ship it
...
rawEscapeByteLinesInList=1 rawEscapeByteLinesInShow=6

=== AFTER (this patch, identical inputs, head 7ee6df2a21) ===
--- seed: real import -> TranscriptsStore -> writeSummary (no session descriptor) ---
{"summaryWrittenTo":".../transcripts/2026-07-16/ansi--31mprovider-0m/summary.md","summaryInOriginalDir":true}
--- openclaw transcripts list ---
2026-07-16/ansi--31mprovider-0m	2026-07-16T10:00:00.000Z	Q3 Board sync	.../summary.md
--- copied selector from list: 2026-07-16/ansi--31mprovider-0m ---
--- openclaw transcripts show <selector> ---
# Q3 Board sync
...
Session: ansi-provider
## Overview
ADMIN APPROVED decision: ship it
...
--- openclaw transcripts path <selector> ---
.../transcripts/2026-07-16/ansi--31mprovider-0m/summary.md
rawEscapeByteLinesInList=0 rawEscapeByteLinesInShow=0
```

Before the patch, `list` and `show` replay the raw ESC bytes (screen clear `^[[2J` plus color spoofing) into the terminal. After the patch, no escape byte reaches the terminal, the summary written without a descriptor still lands in the original session directory with its raw `sessionId` preserved in `summary.json`, and the selector printed by `list` resolves through both `show` and `path`.

Regression coverage: `src/transcripts/summary.test.ts` proves CSI, OSC 8, and C1 CSI sequences are stripped from rendered content while `summary.sessionId` keeps the raw provider ID and the rendered `Session:` line is sanitized; `src/transcripts/store.test.ts` proves `writeSummary` without a session descriptor stores the summary in the existing session directory for an ANSI-bearing session ID; `src/cli/program/register.transcripts.test.ts` drives import through the manual provider and store, asserts `show` and `list` output carry no ESC bytes, covers legacy summaries at the `show` boundary, and round-trips the printed `list` selector through `show` and `path`.

Local gates on the changed files: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/transcripts/summary.test.ts src/transcripts/store.test.ts src/cli/program/register.transcripts.test.ts src/agents/tools/transcripts-tool.test.ts` (35 passed on the rebased head), `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed files, `git diff --check` clean.

Not tested: live capture providers emitting escape bytes through `onUtterance` (the same summary build path covers them); no full build was run.

target.title: fix(auth-profiles): bound auth-profile JSON reads with size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The internal `readJsonFile` function in `source-check.ts` reads auth-profile JSON files with no size bound. A corrupted or hostile auth-profiles.json could exhaust memory when the runtime checks for available credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readJsonFile` previously used raw `fs.readFileSync(pathname, "utf8")` with no size check. The fix reads through `readRegularFileSync` (imported via the `src/infra/regular-file.ts` policy wrapper, per the fs-safe import boundary) with a descriptor-level 10 MiB cap:

1. The path is first resolved with `fs.realpathSync`, so symlinked auth stores (dotfile-manager setups) keep working exactly as they did under `readFileSync` — the established file contract is preserved, while non-regular resolved targets are still rejected.
2. The resolved target is opened once and inspected via its descriptor, binding the size check to the file actually being read (no stat-then-read TOCTOU race).
3. Files exceeding 10 MiB are rejected and return null, same as other read failures — silent skip with no credentials detected, and the caller surfaces its normal "no credential source" guidance.

## User Impact

- Prevents OOM crashes from oversized auth-profile stores
- All existing behavior preserved for normal-sized files, including stores reached through symlinks (current `auth-profiles.json` and legacy `auth.json`)
- Oversized stores are safely skipped before read; the process keeps running and the CLI reports its standard "no credentials found" guidance
- No user-visible change in credential detection results

target.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `saveCronQuarantineFile` function archives overflowing quarantine sidecar files using timestamped unique filenames, but repeated overflow recovery can accumulate unlimited archive files on disk, causing unbounded disk growth.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper review flagged unbounded archive growth as a merge risk. Each overflow event creates a new archive file (`{quarantinePath}.{timestamp}.{random}.archive.json`), and without a retention policy, repeated recovery cycles could exhaust disk space.

## What Changed

- Added `CRON_QUARANTINE_MAX_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024` constant for bounded reads
- `loadCronQuarantineFile` uses `readRegularFile` with `maxBytes` — descriptor-level bounded read (replaces unbounded `fs.promises.readFile`)
- `saveCronQuarantineFile` detects existing files over 8 MiB, archives them via rename, and starts a fresh sidecar
- Archive filename shape: `{quarantinePath}.{timestamp}.{random}.archive.json`
- **No auto-pruning** — all archives are retained for operator inspection. The bounded read/write cap (8 MiB per file) naturally limits disk growth per overflow cycle. Automatic deletion of recovery archives requires maintainer approval.

## User Impact

- Prevents OOM from corrupted oversized quarantine sidecar files
- On overflow, the existing sidecar is archived and a fresh one is started — cron writes continue
- No recovery data is silently deleted; all archives are preserved
- Each active or archived sidecar is individually bounded at 8 MiB

## Evidence (head SHA: `67f8bdd40a3`)

### Full Test Suite — `pnpm test src/cron/store.test.ts` — 52/52 pass ✓

target.title: fix: Control UI avatar initial breaks on emoji display names
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent's display name begins with an emoji or other astral Unicode character, the Control UI renders a broken/garbled avatar initial (a lone UTF-16 surrogate half) instead of the intended glyph, because the fallback uses `.slice(0, 1)` / `[0]` (first UTF-16 code unit).

## Summary

- **Solution**: one shared grapheme-boundary owner — `takeGraphemes` in `ui/src/lib/grapheme.ts` (`Intl.Segmenter`, `granularity: "grapheme"`, with a code-point fallback) — consumed by both the existing plugin monogram (`ui/src/pages/plugins/presentation.ts`, replacing its local copy) and `deriveAvatarInitial` (`ui/src/lib/avatar.ts`). No second grapheme implementation remains.
- **The four live avatar fallback surfaces** now route through that owner via `deriveAvatarInitial(...) || "?"`:
  - `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — sidebar agent card avatar
  - `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-agent-menu.ts` — agent menu row initial
  - `ui/src/components/agent-select.ts` — agent selector dropdown fallback
  - `ui/src/pages/agents/panels-overview.ts` — agents overview identity editor avatar
- **Rebased onto current `main`** (`556a2ee276f`, single commit). The upstream sidebar refactor renamed the chip to `openclaw-sidebar-agent-card`; the fix was reapplied at the new `cardAvatarText` site and the E2E selectors were updated to match (`sidebar-agent-card__main`, `sidebar-agent-card__avatar-text`).
- **What did NOT change**: ASCII names render identically; no behavior change to avatar URLs or the plugin monogram output.

## Evidence

**Live Control UI/Gateway proof** (no mocks): real built CLI (`pnpm install && pnpm build`, `node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 18991`) with an isolated scratch state dir and a config declaring two agents (`main` = "Main", `emoji` = "🚀Rocket"). A real Chromium session (Playwright, no mocked Gateway) authenticated with a scratch loopback token read the rendered DOM of each surface. Terminal trace:

```text
$ node capture-live-proof.mjs   # drives http://127.0.0.1:18991/ (real gateway)
{
  "menuAvatar": "🚀",      // sidebar agent menu row (wa-dropdown-item[value="agent:emoji"])
  "cardAvatar": "🚀",      // sidebar agent card after switching to the emoji agent
  "selectAvatar": "M",     // agent-select trigger shows the selected agent (Main)
  "overviewAvatar": "🚀",  // agents overview identity editor
  "errors": []
}
$ node recapture-select.mjs      // agents page dropdown, open state
{"itemAvatar":"🚀"}             // agent-select dropdown item for 🚀Rocket
```

Redacted screenshots from the same live session (loopback gateway, scratch config, no real endpoints/credentials):

- Sidebar agent menu: https://github.com/xydigit-zt/xydigit-zt-openclaw/releases/download/pr-104912-proof/live-01-agent-menu.png
- Sidebar agent card after switching to 🚀Rocket: https://github.com/xydigit-zt/xydigit-zt-openclaw/releases/download/pr-104912-proof/live-02-sidebar-card.png
- Agents page selector dropdown: https://github.com/xydigit-zt/xydigit-zt-openclaw/releases/download/pr-104912-proof/live-03-agent-select.png
- Agents overview identity editor: https://github.com/xydigit-zt/xydigit-zt-openclaw/releases/download/pr-104912-proof/live-04-agents-overview.png

**Mocked-Gateway Chromium E2E** (deterministic regression lane, real browser DOM asserted `.toBe("🚀")` on all four surfaces):

```text
$ OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts \
    ui/src/e2e/avatar-initial-emoji.e2e.test.ts
✓ renders the emoji grapheme initial in the sidebar chip and agent menu row
✓ renders the emoji grapheme initial in the agent selector dropdown
✓ renders the emoji grapheme initial in the agents overview identity editor
Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  3 passed (3)
```

**Unit + component tests**:

```text
$ pnpm test ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts ui/src/lib/grapheme.test.ts ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts
Test Files  3 passed (3)   Tests  23 passed (23)
```

`pnpm tsgo:ui` exit 0; `oxfmt`/`oxlint` clean on touched files; `git diff --check` clean.

## Regression Test Plan

- `ui/src/lib/grapheme.test.ts` — shared slicer: ASCII, emoji, ZWJ family, flags, skin-tone, empty input, plus the `Intl.Segmenter`-unavailable code-point fallback (fresh module import under stub).
- `ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts` — `deriveAvatarInitial` behavior via the shared owner.
- `ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts` — component fallback keeps the full cluster (`👨‍👩‍👧‍👦`).
- `ui/src/e2e/avatar-initial-emoji.e2e.test.ts` — all four live surfaces in real Chromium.

What was not tested: every possible Unicode boundary was not enumerated; the proof targets the four known live `.slice(0,1)`/`[0]` avatar-initial surfaces and the documented fallback path. The plugin monogram's rendered output is unchanged (same algorithm, shared source).

target.title: refactor(whatsapp): centralize inbound turn admission and history finalization
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp duplicated two responsibilities already owned by the shared channel turn machinery: translating an SDK ingress decision into turn admission, and clearing pending group history after reply dispatch.

Keeping those decisions in the plugin made the WhatsApp receive path easier to drift from the core turn lifecycle.

## What Changed

- Derive the canonical turn admission from the resolved SDK ingress decision at the WhatsApp access-control boundary.
- Preserve the shipped, redacted `senderAccess`, `commandAccess`, and `activationAccess` callback projections while adding `turnAdmission`. The complete resolved ingress object and its effective allowlists remain private.
- Export the decision-only admission mapper through `channel-ingress-runtime`, the modern receive-path SDK owner.
- Carry admission and group-history finalization options as data on the current `ChannelTurnPlan` returned through `runChannelInboundEvent`.
- Let the core turn executor finalize pending group history after successful dispatch, and remove WhatsApp's duplicate clearing branches from the reply finalizer.
- Construct the deprecated flat-message admission directly instead of fabricating an SDK ingress graph for a compatibility path that predates it.

Broadcast behavior is unchanged: each agent receives the same pending-history snapshot, per-agent core finalization is suppressed, and the existing broadcast barrier clears the shared history once after fan-out finishes.

## Behavior and Compatibility

Reachable behavior remains unchanged:

- Successful dispatches clear pending group history for both silent and visible replies.
- Observe-only turns suppress transport delivery and retain pending group history.
- Failed dispatches retain pending group history.
- Existing callback consumers continue to receive the shipped redacted access projections.

## Evidence

- Focused Plugin SDK mapper and WhatsApp admission, dispatch, process-message, and broadcast tests
- Plugin SDK API-baseline and surface checks
- WhatsApp extension typecheck
- Production build, including Plugin SDK declaration and export verification

target.title: fix(agents): race in-flight tool promises against run abort (#103905)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103905. When an embedded run aborts, a **non-cooperative** in-flight tool — one whose `execute` never observes the abort signal (e.g. stuck waiting on a subprocess) — keeps the wrapped call pending forever. The run then hangs instead of failing fast, leaving sessions stuck.

## Why This Change Was Made

`wrapToolWithAbortSignal` (in `src/agents/agent-tools.abort.ts`, the wrapper imported by `src/agents/agent-tools.ts` on current main) now races the tool's execute promise against the combined abort signal:

- On abort, the wrapped call **rejects immediately** with an `AbortError` instead of awaiting the tool forever.
- JavaScript cannot cancel a running promise: a non-cooperative tool keeps executing in the background and may settle later, but that late settlement is detached so the result never lands in an aborted run.
- Tool settlements pass through untouched, preserving tool error semantics.

**File note for reviewers:** an earlier review asked to port the race to `src/agents/pi-tools.abort.ts`. Current main has since renamed that file to `src/agents/agent-tools.abort.ts` (#85341 "internalize OpenClaw agent runtime"), so this PR's rebased diff now lands on the **active** wrapper — verified: `src/agents/agent-tools.ts:28` imports `wrapToolWithAbortSignal` from `./agent-tools.abort.js`.

## User Impact

Aborted runs reject promptly instead of hanging on stuck tool calls; normal tool results are unaffected.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof — live abort race (final head `f9f61c2e`, 2026-07-19).

The real `wrapToolWithAbortSignal` was executed via `tsx` (no mocks of the wrapper; a tool stub stands in only for the tool itself):

```bash
./node_modules/.bin/tsx abort-race-proof.mts
```

```text
date: Sun Jul 19 2026 07:58:49 GMT+0800 (中国标准时间)
node: v24.18.0
code path: src/agents/agent-tools.abort.ts wrapToolWithAbortSignal @ PR head
[non-cooperative] rejected in 101ms after abort: name=AbortError message="Aborted"
[late-settling] aborted call rejected in 101ms: Aborted
[late-settling] background tool later settled=true (detached from aborted run)
[normal] resolved with tool result: {"echoed":{"hello":"world"}}
[result] PASS: abort races in-flight tool promises; normal results unaffected
```

- **Non-cooperative tool** (execute promise never settles): rejects 101ms after the 100ms abort — without the race this call would hang forever.
- **Late-settling tool**: the aborted call rejects promptly; the background tool still settles later (400ms), detached from the aborted run.
- **Normal tool**: result passes through unchanged.

Regression tests (final head):

```bash
pnpm vitest run src/agents/agent-tools.abort.test.ts
```

```text
Tests  14 passed (14)
```

## What was not tested

A full embedded-agent run with a live model provider; the proof exercises the exact wrapper whose await-vs-race behavior this PR changes.

## Rebase status

Rebased onto latest `origin/main` at head `f9f61c2e`; the rename of `pi-tools.abort.ts` → `agent-tools.abort.ts` means the rebased diff targets the active wrapper on current main.

target.title: fix(scripts): startup fixture refresh no longer hangs on stalled benchmarks
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where contributors refreshing the checked-in CLI startup benchmark fixture could wait forever when the benchmark driver stalled during argument parsing, module loading, report persistence, or final cleanup. The existing `--timeout-ms` option bounded individual measured CLI runs only; the updater's outer wait for the benchmark driver had no deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

The updater now supervises the benchmark driver with a hard total deadline derived from the selected preset's case count, measured and warmup runs, each per-run timeout, both internal timeout-cleanup windows, and additional driver cleanup grace. It first asks the driver to terminate, then escalates to a force kill and a final bounded settle phase even if no child `close` event arrives.

The driver writes to a temporary output that is published only after status 0, so a timeout after report persistence cannot replace or truncate the checked-in fixture. A missing destination uses sibling staging and is atomically created; an existing regular destination uses a private system-temporary staging directory and is written through its resolved final inode, preserving symlinks, hardlinks, restricted permissions, ownership, and ACLs without requiring parent-directory write or file read access. Named pipes, devices, and other special outputs are rejected before the benchmark instead of being replaced. The updater and driver also handle the standard POSIX termination set including `SIGQUIT`, with conventional signal exit codes. The benchmark driver reports its active detached sample process-group leader over a private IPC channel, allowing the updater to kill that group directly after timeout, interruption, or any independent driver close. CLI flags, benchmark defaults, fixture schema, and the separate budget-check command are unchanged; that sibling command's independent deadline fix is tracked in #110923.

## User Impact

Startup fixture refreshes now fail nonzero instead of hanging indefinitely when the benchmark driver stalls. Failed, timed-out, or interrupted refreshes preserve the previous fixture, remove temporary output, and do not leave an active measured CLI process behind. Healthy benchmark runs retain their full modeled execution and cleanup budget, including when a custom regular output is reached through symlinks or hardlinks or has restricted permissions.

## Evidence

- Red regressions before the complete fix reproduced both failure modes: a driver that wrote output and then hung replaced the destination fixture, and terminating a driver with an active detached sample left the sample group running.
- Independent issue-path runtime after the fix: the real updater exited with status 1 after 22,119 ms against a driver that wrote output, ignored `SIGTERM`, and reported an active detached sample group; the proof supervisor did not time out, the existing fixture was unchanged, temporary output was removed, and both the sample leader and descendant were gone. A real benchmark driver also exited with status 143 after responsive termination, with its sample group fully reaped.
- Regression suite: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/test-projects.mjs test/scripts/test-update-cli-startup-bench.test.ts test/scripts/bench-cli-startup.test.ts test/scripts/cli-startup-bench-spawner.test.ts` — 41 tests passed, including a mocked child that never emits `close` after force kill and an independent driver-crash cleanup case; custom-output symlink, hardlink, dangling-target, cycle, `0600`, read-only, write-only, restricted-directory, FIFO, and device coverage; and real `SIGQUIT` driver/sample-group cleanup with exit 131.
- Formatting: `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check scripts/test-update-cli-startup-bench.mjs scripts/bench-cli-startup.ts test/scripts/test-update-cli-startup-bench.test.ts test/scripts/bench-cli-startup.test.ts test/scripts/cli-startup-bench-spawner.test.ts`.
- Targeted lint passed for the changed updater, benchmark driver, and regression tests.
- Fresh same-problem recall found no open PR covering this fixture-updater deadline.

target.title: fix(clawhub): preserve legacy telemetry opt-out behind blank primary env
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled for this PR.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users opting out of ClawHub install telemetry through the supported legacy `CLAWDHUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY` variable could still send an install event when `CLAWHUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY` was also present but blank.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telemetry opt-out resolution now ignores blank values before applying the existing primary-then-legacy precedence. The accepted opt-out values and telemetry payload remain unchanged.

## User Impact

A valid legacy telemetry opt-out remains effective even when an empty primary variable is injected by an environment file or launcher.

## Evidence

Exact base: `ec740e79a48c1d7879fe3e8f211b4f0719d5ec0e`
Exact head: `d68ff63d982b00eb9d1a13bc3c52b6790cdd7a31`
Node: `v24.18.0`

The regression calls `reportClawHubSkillInstallTelemetry()` with a real request seam. Before the production change:

    expected fetchImpl not to be called
    received one POST /api/cli/telemetry/install
    Tests  1 failed | 79 passed | 2 skipped (82)

After:

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/clawhub.test.ts
    Test Files  1 passed (1)
    Tests  80 passed | 2 skipped (82)

Targeted oxfmt and `git diff --check` also passed. The test asserts that the request is never emitted when the primary value is blank and the supported legacy opt-out is true.

AI-assisted: Codex helped identify, implement, and validate this fix; I verified the code and evidence.


### Native request-path proof

At exact head `d68ff63d982b00eb9d1a13bc3c52b6790cdd7a31`, I invoked the production `reportClawHubSkillInstallTelemetry()` entry with its default native `fetch` transport against a loopback HTTP server. The first run used a blank primary variable plus the legacy opt-out; the control run removed both variables to prove the real endpoint and transport were active:

    {"head":"d68ff63d982b00eb9d1a13bc3c52b6790cdd7a31","entry":"reportClawHubSkillInstallTelemetry","transport":"native fetch to loopback HTTP server","blankPrimary":"   ","legacyOptOut":"true","optedOutRequests":0,"controlRequests":[{"method":"POST","path":"/api/cli/telemetry/install"}]}

The opt-out run emitted zero requests. The control immediately reached the same server with one `POST /api/cli/telemetry/install`, demonstrating that the zero count came from the production opt-out path rather than a disconnected request seam. The proof used only a synthetic token and loopback traffic.

target.title: fix(ui): prevent stale sidebar attention refreshes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing sidebar health alerts could see cron or model-auth state revert when an older refresh on the same gateway connection completed after a newer refresh. The stale completion could also prune persisted dismissals against obsolete data and make an alert reappear unexpectedly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each sidebar attention load now owns a generation token. Starting a replacement load, disconnecting, or detaching the component retires earlier generations, so only the current load may project cron/auth state, update the freshness timestamp, or prune dismissals.

## User Impact

Sidebar health alerts now remain based on the newest completed refresh during slow or overlapping gateway requests. This is a race-condition fix with no visual or configuration changes.

## Evidence

- Added a component-level deferred-request regression that starts two loads on the same client, completes the newer load first, then proves the older load cannot overwrite cron state, auth state, `loadedAtMs`, or persisted dismissals.
- Exact-head upstream CI is green on `32acfbf7d2e68795593a68fb7e38be037d9fa082`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29666771483
- Real Chromium before/after proof uses the actual Lit component and application context with one deterministic gateway client. The workflow pins current-main before SHA `b550c2cf9a8afff68958f98d71aa7e3c939f3e39` and PR after SHA `32acfbf7d2e68795593a68fb7e38be037d9fa082`: https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/actions/runs/29667390493
- Before: request B completes first, then stale request A restores cron `stale` and auth timestamp `1`, deletes the persisted dismissal, and visibly restores `1 cron job(s) failed`.
- After: request B remains authoritative after A completes: cron `current`, auth timestamp `2`, the B freshness timestamp is unchanged, the `cronFailed: current` dismissal remains, and the visible alert stays absent.
- Redacted proof artifact contains the before/after PNG screenshots and WebM recordings: https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/actions/runs/29667390493/artifacts/8436164573
- `git diff --check` passes on the exact PR head.
- Independent Codex adversarial review of the frozen diff found 0 actionable findings, including explicit disconnect, detach, and same-client reconnect lifecycle review.

AI-assisted: Codex was used for implementation, independent review, and deterministic browser proof; I reviewed and understand the change.

target.title: feat(policy): check authored message routing
target.body:
Closes #111050

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators could not express or continuously verify message-routing intent in the Policy plugin. A stale binding channel id, empty binding set, or unexpected fallback could silently route inbound messages to the default agent while `policy check` remained clean.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds opt-in routing conformance to the bundled Policy plugin without changing core config validation, gateway startup, runtime routing, or fallback behavior. Operators author structural requirements and representative route probes in `policy.jsonc`; Policy evaluates those probes with OpenClaw's public runtime resolver.

Routing evidence is deliberately redacted. It records binding indexes and channel ids plus each authored probe's id, resolved agent, and match kind. It does not serialize peer, account, guild, team, role, session, or binding-destination identifiers. Routing findings are review-required and never automatically rewrite bindings.

## User Impact

Operators can now require at least one route binding, reject bindings whose channel is absent from configured `channels.*`, and assert that representative inbound routes resolve to an expected agent at an expected binding specificity.

Existing policies are unchanged unless they add a `routing` section. Policies without routing retain the same evidence shape and attestation hashes.

## Evidence

Isolated dev fixtures used synthetic ids, disabled channels, temporary state, and explicit build paths. No production config, gateway, LaunchAgent, or live message traffic was touched.

| Scenario | Installed dev baseline | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Empty bindings, no routing policy | Clean Policy result | Clean Policy result with identical policy/workspace/findings/attestation hashes |
| Routing policy present | `policy/policy-jsonc-invalid` because `routing` is unsupported | Supported |
| Healthy peer binding and fallback | Detective script clean | Policy clean |
| Empty bindings | Detective script fails | `routing-bindings-required`, `routing-agent-mismatch`, `routing-match-kind-mismatch` |
| Retired `bluebubbles` binding | Detective script fails | `routing-binding-channel-unconfigured` plus probe mismatch findings |
| Privileged default fallback | Detective script fails | `routing-agent-mismatch` and `routing-match-kind-mismatch` |

Additional proof:

- `policy check --json` emitted no seeded peer or group identifiers.
- `doctor --lint --json` emitted the same routing findings.
- 357 focused Policy tests passed, including CLI compare, Doctor registration, schema, evidence privacy, and all four incident fixtures.
- `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, and `lint:extensions` passed using the trusted-source local fallback after the delegated Testbox wrapper duplicated dispatches.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Codex autoreview was run repeatedly and all accepted findings were fixed. Its final scoped-routing claim was rejected because scoped policy validation explicitly disallows `routing`, routing metadata declares no scope selectors, and the scoped docs table excludes it.

target.title: fix(sms): isolate validated webhook quotas per sender
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The SMS webhook's accepted-callback quota was keyed by resolved client address. Twilio shares egress addresses across unrelated senders, so one flooding sender could exhaust the 30/minute callback budget and make valid callbacks from other users fail with HTTP 429.

## Why This Change Was Made

The patch keeps the existing pre-validation failed-request budget keyed by account, route, and client address, then uses two post-validation limits: sender fairness plus bounded account/route admission.

- Signature-validated callbacks use `resolveTwilioInboundSender(form)`, so equivalent SMS and `RCS:` address forms share one sender bucket.
- A true single-sender overload remains observable as HTTP 429; the handler does not acknowledge and silently discard it.
- Another validated sender behind the same Twilio egress address remains dispatchable.
- All validated senders on an account/route share a 300/minute aggregate ceiling, so high-cardinality signed fan-out cannot create unbounded durable-ingress pressure.
- With `dangerouslyDisableSignatureValidation`, `From` is unauthenticated, so the stricter callback budget stays keyed to the resolved client address and cannot be bypassed by rotating sender text.

## User Impact

One abusive or bursty sender can no longer cross-throttle unrelated SMS users behind Twilio's shared infrastructure. The existing 30/minute sender threshold and invalid-request behavior remain unchanged, while the new 300/minute account/route ceiling keeps aggregate overload fail-closed and visible.

The 10:1 aggregate-to-sender ratio permits multiple active senders without recreating the shared-egress bug, while preserving an explicit absolute ceiling for durable ingress.

## Evidence

Current contributor head: `bdd8173fd6a` on upstream `main` `aad27e26296`.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/sms/src/webhook.test.ts`: 13/13 passed, including the sender-isolation and aggregate fan-out regressions.
- Positive regression: 30 callbacks from sender A are accepted; sender B on the same egress address is still accepted.
- Negative regression: sender A's 31st callback returns 429 even when its address changes from SMS E.164 syntax to equivalent `RCS:+1 (555) 123-4567` syntax and even when the egress IP changes.
- Signature-disabled regression: rotating `From` values does not widen the address-keyed quota.
- Invalid/missing canonical senders share an empty-sender bucket without consuming a valid sender's quota.
- High-cardinality regression: 300 distinct signed senders are accepted on one account/route and the 301st returns 429 without enqueueing.
- Fixed-window recovery regression: the sender becomes dispatchable after the window expires.
- Direct formatter check and `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- The pre-PR plan gate passed for extension, extension-test, and docs lanes with no dependency-sensitive changes.

### Real behavior proof

The focused suite drives the real request-body parser, Twilio HMAC validation, canonical sender resolver, fixed-window limiter, response writer, and durable-ingress seam with realistic HTTP requests. It proves both the intended isolation and the closest bypasses without deploying the Gateway.

No live Twilio callback was sent to this exact branch head, and no Gateway restart or production webhook change was performed. A maintainer-controlled live Twilio smoke remains the strongest optional transport proof.

AI-assisted; reviewed and validated before submission.
